title: Paprikas Krumpli
subtitle: Hungarian paprika potato stew
excerpt: A deeply coloured Hungarian potato stew made with sweet and hot paprika, onion, and a generous spoonful of soured cream stirred in at the end. Fast to make and built from very few ingredients.
sourceNotes: A classic Hungarian peasant dish, eaten widely across the country. Made with the same paprika-onion base used in gulyas and porkolt.

recipe.freezeNotes: Potato stews do not freeze well as the potato texture changes on defrosting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made fresh. You can prepare the onion base up to 2 hours ahead and add the potatoes when ready to finish.

content.text: Paprikas krumpli is a Hungarian potato stew with a red paprika-onion base and a spoonful of soured cream. Use a waxy potato so the pieces hold their shape. Take the pan off the heat before adding the soured cream or it will split.

items.prepNote: waxy variety, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

content.text: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Take the pan off the heat. Add the sweet paprika and stir quickly. Return to a low heat. This step prevents the paprika from burning.
Add the garlic and red pepper. Cook for 3 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes until the tomatoes begin to break apart.
Add the potatoes and pour in the stock. The liquid should just cover the potatoes; add water if needed.
Bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has reduced.
Season well with salt. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the soured cream. Do not return to the heat or the cream will split.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

items.cause: It was added to the hot pan and scorched.
items.fix: Always take the pan off the heat before adding paprika. Stir it into the warm onions away from the flame.

items.cause: The cream was stirred in while the stew was still boiling.
items.fix: Remove from the heat and let it settle for a minute before adding the soured cream.

items.cause: A floury potato was used instead of a waxy one, or they cooked too long.
items.fix: Use a waxy variety such as Charlotte or new potatoes. Check from 18 minutes and stop cooking as soon as a knife goes in easily.
